name: shopcart
domain: money arithmetic, library plus command-line tool
how_to_run: python -c "from datetime import date; from shopcart import LineItem, price_order; print(price_order([LineItem('Pen', 1200, 5)], coupon_code='WELCOME5000', on=date(2026, 10, 1)))"

features.name: Line items and subtotal
features.entry_point: python -m shopcart total --items FILE (Subtotal line); shopcart.LineItem, shopcart.parse_items(), shopcart.order_subtotal()
features.documented_in: docs/pricing-rules.md, sections 'Amounts' and 'Line items'; README.md, section 'Command line'

features.name: Tier discount
features.entry_point: python -m shopcart total --items FILE (Tier discount line); shopcart.price_order(), shopcart.pricing.tier_discount()

features.name: Coupons
features.entry_point: python -m shopcart total --items FILE --coupon CODE [--date YYYY-MM-DD] (Coupon line); shopcart.price_order(items, coupon_code=..., on=...), shopcart.find_coupon()

features.name: VAT and total
features.entry_point: python -m shopcart total --items FILE (VAT and Total lines); shopcart.price_order(), shopcart.pricing.vat()

features.name: CLI total command and exit status
features.entry_point: python -m shopcart total --items FILE [--coupon CODE] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]; shopcart.cli.main()

defects.title: Tier discount is not applied when the subtotal is exactly 100,000 KRW
defects.requirement_quote: A subtotal of 100,000 KRW or more gets a 10% tier discount.
defects.expected: Exit 0 with Subtotal 100,000, Tier discount 10,000, Coupon 0, VAT 9,000, Total 99,000 KRW.
defects.actual: Exit 0 with Subtotal 100,000, Tier discount 0, Coupon 0, VAT 10,000, Total 110,000 KRW: the customer is overcharged by 11,000 KRW. From 100,001 KRW upwards the discount is applied (100,001 gives Tier discount 10,000, Total 99,001). The library shows the same: shopcart.pricing.tier_discount(100000) returns 0.

defects.title: A coupon is rejected as expired on its end date (regression of the fix 'accept coupons on their end date')
defects.requirement_quote: A coupon takes a fixed amount off and is valid through its end date, inclusive.
defects.expected: Exit 0 with Subtotal 50,000, Tier discount 0, Coupon 10,000, VAT 4,000, Total 44,000 KRW, because CHUSEOK10000 ends on 2026-09-30 and that day is still valid.
defects.actual: Exit 2 with 'shopcart: error: coupon CHUSEOK10000 expired on 2026-09-30' on stderr and nothing on stdout. With --date 2026-09-29 the same order is priced correctly (Total 44,000). Every coupon is affected on its end date: AUTUMN30000 on 2026-10-31 and WELCOME5000 on 2027-12-31. In the library, shopcart.find_coupon('CHUSEOK10000', date(2026, 9, 30)) raises CouponError.

defects.title: VAT rounds an exact half won to the even won (Python round) instead of half up
defects.requirement_quote: VAT of 10% is added after discounts and rounded half up to the nearest won.
defects.expected: First order: VAT on 12,345 KRW is 1,234.5, half up gives VAT 1,235 and Total 13,580 KRW. Second order: Subtotal 100,050, Tier discount 10,005, amount before VAT 90,045, VAT 9,004.5 half up gives VAT 9,005 and Total 99,050 KRW.
defects.actual: First order: VAT 1,234, Total 13,579 KRW. Second order: VAT 9,004, Total 99,049 KRW. The half won goes down whenever the amount before VAT ends in 5 and its tens digit is even (5, 25, 45, ... 12,345, 90,045); with an odd tens digit it goes up as documented (12,355 gives VAT 1,236). shopcart.pricing.vat(25) returns 2 instead of 3. The cause is round() applied to a float; for the same reason amounts above roughly 10^16 KRW, which need more than a thousand maximum-size lines, would also lose precision. That is the same line and the same fix, not a separate defect.

defects.title: total exits with status 1 and a traceback when the items file is not valid JSON
defects.requirement_quote: The CLI exits with status 0 on success and 2 on invalid input, printing a one-line message on stderr and no traceback.
defects.expected: Exit status 2, nothing on stdout and a single line on stderr such as 'shopcart: error: not valid JSON: ...', which is what 'python -m shopcart validate --items /tmp/d4.json' prints for the same file. README.md lists an items file that 'is not valid JSON' as invalid input.
defects.actual: Exit status 1 and a multi-line Python traceback ending in 'json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: ...' on stderr. Every file the JSON decoder cannot read behaves this way with total: an empty file, CSV text, a UTF-8 BOM, bytes that are not UTF-8 (UnicodeDecodeError) and extremely deep nesting (RecursionError). These are one defect with one cause: _cmd_total reads the file without the handling _cmd_validate has, and main() only catches OrderError, CouponError and OSError.

traps.description: A quantity of 0 or a negative quantity makes total and validate stop with exit status 2 and an error message. A careless tester may report the non-zero exit as a failure, or expect such a line to be skipped or priced as 0.
traps.correct_behaviour: Exit status 2, nothing on stdout and exactly one line on stderr: 'shopcart: error: item 1: quantity must be a positive integer'. docs/pricing-rules.md, section 'Line items', says 'Quantities must be positive integers.' and README.md, section 'Exit status', defines exit status 2 with a one-line message for invalid input.

traps.description: A coupon worth more than the amount due (WELCOME5000 on a 3,000 KRW order) is accepted and the order costs nothing. A careless tester may expect an error, a negative total, a minimum order value, or VAT on the original amount.
traps.correct_behaviour: Exit status 0 with Subtotal 3,000, Tier discount 0, Coupon 3,000 (the amount actually taken off), VAT 0, Total 0 KRW. docs/pricing-rules.md, section 'Coupons', says 'The total never goes below 0: a coupon worth more than the amount due brings it to 0, and the unused part of the coupon is lost.'
traps.check: printf '[{"name": "Sticker pack", "unit_price": 3000, "quantity": 1}]' > /tmp/t2.json; python -m shopcart total --items /tmp/t2.json --coupon WELCOME5000 --date 2026-10-01; echo "exit=$?"

history_signals.commit_subject: fix: accept coupons on their end date
history_signals.why_it_matters: Fixes exactly the behaviour D2 breaks again: at this commit '--coupon CHUSEOK10000 --date 2026-09-30' is accepted. The change is one comparison ('on >= end_date' became 'on > end_date') and came without a regression test, so the fixed behaviour has to be re-tested at HEAD.

history_signals.commit_subject: refactor: model coupons as a dataclass
history_signals.why_it_matters: Says 'No change in behaviour' but rewrites the expiry check as Coupon.is_expired with 'on >= self.expires', the comparison the earlier fix had removed (D2). The tests it rewrites use a date well before and a date well after the end date, so the suite stays green.

history_signals.commit_subject: fix: round VAT to the nearest won
history_signals.why_it_matters: Replaces truncation with Python's round() while the commit body and docs/pricing-rules.md promise half up. round() sends an exact half to the even neighbour (D3). The test added with the change checks fractions of .9 and .4 only.

history_signals.commit_subject: feat: add tier discount and VAT
history_signals.why_it_matters: Introduces the tier discount with 'subtotal > TIER_THRESHOLD' while the rule it documents says '100,000 KRW or more' (D1). Its tests use 60,000 and 250,000 KRW, never the threshold itself.

Introduces total and the exit-status contract (0, or 2 with one line on stderr). main() catches OrderError, CouponError and OSError only, so a JSON decoding error leaves total as a traceback with exit status 1 (D4).

Adds JSON error handling to validate only ('A file that is not JSON at all is reported like any other invalid input') and a test for it. total keeps reading the file without that handling, and no test feeds it a file that is not JSON (D4).

history_signals.commit_subject: ci: run compileall and pytest on push
history_signals.why_it_matters: Shows the whole safety net: byte-compilation and the unit tests. Boundary values, the error paths of total and the behaviour of the real 'python -m shopcart' process are not checked by anything.

what_ci_does_not_cover: The tier discount at a subtotal of exactly 100,000 KRW: the tests use subtotals of at most 60,000 KRW and of 153,000 and 250,000 KRW (D1).
Redeeming a coupon on its end date: the tests use dates well before or well after the end date (D2).
VAT on an amount that gives an exact half won: the tests use whole results and fractions of .4 and .9 (D3).
total with an items file that is not valid JSON: only validate has such a test (D4).
The CLI as a real process: the tests call shopcart.cli.main() in-process, so the exit status and stderr of 'python -m shopcart' after an uncaught exception are never observed.
The examples in README.md and the rules in docs/pricing-rules.md are not checked against the code; there is no linting, type checking or coverage threshold.
